selection_protocol: All model selection used validation macro-F1 ONLY (raw logits; logit-bias tuning logged as diagnostic and never used for selection). Grid: 32 loss x sampling x noise configs per encoder arm at fixed lr=1e-4, dropout=0.2 (from prior P6 evidence), softmax/CORAL heads. Top-4 generic configs then trained with seeds 42/123/456 and ranked by MEAN validation macro-F1. Winner frozen, then evaluated on test exactly once.

final_model.architecture: EfficientNet-B0 + DistilBERT + Adaptive Gated Fusion v3
final_model.encoders: FROZEN generic pretrained (ImageNet / vanilla DistilBERT); never trained on any CrisisMMD sample
final_model.head: softmax

label_quality_and_provenance.review_tiers_note: tiered list produced; NO labels were auto-changed
label_quality_and_provenance.reclaim_contamination_check: byte-level hash distance <=0.10 enforced against all val/test images; 1 sample excluded

leakage_remediation.finding: Original encoders were trained on the pre-cleaning split; 308/436 current test images had been seen by them during training (70.6% inherited leakage). All prior frozen-feature metrics carried indirect leakage.
leakage_remediation.fix: Encoders retrained strictly on the cleaned TRAIN split (2,209 kept + 312 reclaimed = 2,521; zero val/test exposure), then benchmarked against untouched generic pretrained encoders.
leakage_remediation.outcome: Generic frozen encoders WON (higher val macro-F1 than the in-domain fine-tuned arm); final model uses them, which is leakage-free by construction.

ordinal_vs_softmax.conclusion: Ordinal (CORAL-style) heads did NOT outperform the softmax WCE head on validation macro-F1; softmax retained.

inference_times.note: batch size 1, CPU; full pipeline includes both frozen encoders

comparison_vs_historical.caveat: Historical rows were produced with leaky encoders on the same test population; the new row is leakage-free, so the delta is conservative (an apples-to-apples leaky run would score higher).

what_helped_most: 1. Leakage remediation + honest protocol (result is now trustworthy)
2. Controlled search: balanced sampling + inverse-frequency WCE on the wide fusion head
3. Train-set expansion via 312 safely reclaimed low-confidence samples (TRAIN only)

did_full_dataset_help.detail: 14,556 of 18,082 annotation rows lack severity labels and every valid-damage row already carries informative+infrastructure tags, so no hidden supervision exists. The corpus contributed only the 312 reclaimed TRAIN samples. Representation learning over the unlabeled remainder (image SSL / text MLM) was investigated but is infeasible on the available CPU budget within this project's time constraints; it remains the most promising future direction.

limitations: Mild damage is the weakest class (F1 0.41); mild-to-severe confusion dominates errors (51 test samples).
Text tower is weak standalone (encoder-level val macro-F1 0.39 after clean retraining); tweets often lack severity cues.
Validation set is small (460); config ranking carries +-0.02 noise, mitigated by multi-seed mean selection.
The cost-matrix loss diverged in all runs and was excluded.
CPU-only budget prevented self-supervised use of the 14.5k unlabeled samples and longer encoder training.
